outcome: Maternal composite outcome (cesarean deliveries, pre-eclampsia, placental abruption)

Neonatal composite outcome (antenatal or neonatal death, Apgar score at 5 min < 7, admission to the neonatal intensive care unit, need for phototherapy, respiratory abnormalities, birth trauma, neonatal infection)
cohort: The study included 305 women with second trimester HCG >= 2 and/or AFP >= 2 multiples of the median, without additional maternal or fetal complications, from their 38th gestational week.
finding: Early term labor induction in pregnancies with elevated AFP and/or HCG showed a non-significant trend towards improved maternal outcome but significantly increased the rate of mild neonatal morbidity, primarily due to increased phototherapy.
mod_finding: The maternal composite outcome, which included cesarean deliveries, trended towards being twice as high in the expectant management group compared to the labor induction group, though this difference did not reach statistical significance (10% vs 5%).
